【原视频简介】
OpenAI just published an extraordinary 165-page paper claiming to have solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem—one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems that has haunted mathematicians for over two centuries. 

Powered by a synchronized swarm of 10,000 autonomous AI agents running for 88 straight hours, OpenAI proved a finite-time blowup and formally verified the entire proof in Lean 4. But within hours of the announcement, explosive allegations emerged: prominent mathematician Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claim their private Codex work was scooped, igniting an all-out industry war.

In this deep-dive documentary, we break down:
- What the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem actually is
- How Noam Brown's 10,000-agent reasoning swarm found the proof
- Why Lean interactive theorem proving changes mathematical verification forever
- The bitter IP controversy between OpenAI, Tristan Buckmaster, and Anthropic
- Why Sam Altman officially declined the $1,000,000 Clay Mathematics Institute prize
